questions.q: What does 'max degree of parallelism' actually control?
options: How many logical processors a single query's parallel operators can use, not how many queries can run concurrently
The total number of concurrent user connections allowed
The maximum number of databases on the instance
The size of the plan cache
questions.explain: MAXDOP caps the thread span of one query's parallel operators — it has nothing to do with overall concurrency of separate queries.

questions.q: Per Microsoft's guidance in this lesson, what MAXDOP is generally appropriate for a server with multiple NUMA nodes and more than 8 logical processors per node?
options: 8 (or a bit higher, tuned to the workload) — rarely the full per-node or system-wide processor count
The full system-wide logical processor count
Always exactly 1
Always exactly the number of NUMA nodes
questions.explain: The guidance caps around 8 on larger multi-NUMA systems specifically to avoid a single query spanning NUMA node boundaries, which introduces its own latency.

questions.q: What does 'cost threshold for parallelism' control?
options: The estimated plan cost a query must exceed before the optimizer even considers a parallel plan at all
How many logical processors a query can use once it goes parallel
The maximum memory grant a query can request
Whether Query Store captures a query
questions.explain: Below the cost threshold, SQL Server always runs a query serially regardless of the MAXDOP setting; it's a separate gate answering a different question.

questions.q: Why is the default value of 5 for cost threshold for parallelism considered outdated, per this lesson?
options: It was set decades ago on hardware far weaker than modern servers, so cheap queries go parallel unnecessarily and waste CPU on parallelism overhead
It is actually too high for modern hardware and should be lowered
It only applies to Azure SQL Database, not on-prem SQL Server
SQL Server ignores this setting entirely in modern versions
questions.explain: On modern hardware, a threshold of 5 is far too low, letting small, cheap queries go parallel and incur thread-spawning and coordination overhead for no benefit.

questions.q: At what levels can MAXDOP be overridden, per this lesson?
options: Instance-wide with sp_configure, per database (SQL Server 2016+), and per query with a hint
Only instance-wide — no other override exists
Only per query, never instance-wide or per database
Only through the Windows registry
questions.explain: MAXDOP can be set at three levels — sp_configure for the instance default, ALTER DATABASE SET MAXDOP for a database, and OPTION (MAXDOP n) for a single query.
